data.reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed all 6 files and found them safe with detailed reasoning. The qwen model's inconclusive result was due to API errors (HTTP 400) on PKGBUILD and fvwm.desktop, not security concerns. All successfully reviewed files show standard AUR packaging: pinned checksums, legitimate upstream sources (GitHub), routine build-compatibility patches, and a standard desktop entry. No malicious injection patterns, no unpinned sources, no suspicious network operations or code execution during build/install.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from tool failures in the qwen model (API errors on 2/6 files), not from conflicting security assessments. The deepseek model completed a full review and found no issues. This is a coverage problem, not a genuine disagreement about security.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit PKGBUILD and fvwm.desktop due to HTTP 400 API errors, leaving 2/6 files unreviewed
learnings: Implement retry logic or fallback models when API calls fail with transient errors (HTTP 400/500)
Distinguish between 'inconclusive due to tool errors' and 'inconclusive due to genuine uncertainty' in verdict reporting
When one model has tool failures and another completes successfully, weight the successful model's verdict more heavily in adjudication
Track API error rates per model to identify reliability issues
